title: Exceptional drought expands to nearly a quarter of Pontotoc County
excerpt: The share of Pontotoc County in the most intense drought category rose from 13.36% to 22.75% in a week. All of the county remains in severe drought or worse.
locality: Pontotoc County, Mississippi, with statewide comparison.

paragraphs.text: Nearly a quarter of Pontotoc County is now in exceptional drought, the most intense category on the U.S. Drought Monitor’s scale. The map released Thursday puts 22.75% of the county in that category as of Nov. 17, up from 13.36% on Nov. 10.

The change also shows up one step down the scale. Extreme drought or worse now covers 87.77% of the county, up from 74.65% a week earlier. The rest of Pontotoc County is in severe drought. These percentages measure land area, and the extreme-or-worse figure includes the areas in exceptional drought.

Across Mississippi, exceptional drought spread from 7.45% of the state to 27.75% over the same week. That puts the statewide share above Pontotoc County’s. But severe drought or worse still covers a larger share of Pontotoc County than of Mississippi as a whole, where the figure is 80.06%.
